Design decisions

Source: DECISIONS.md

Each entry: id, date, status (approved / proposed / pending), decision, reason. Approved entries are decided by the author.

Approved

  • D-001 (2026-11-20) Package name trainingmodels. Checked with pak::pkg_name_check: valid, free on CRAN and Bioconductor.
  • D-002 (2026-11-18) First version scope: daily-series core, load descriptors, Banister impulse-response model. Later: Busso variable dose-response, fitness delay, Kalman filter, Bayesian version, DLNM via the dlnm package (wrapped, not reimplemented).
  • D-003 (2026-11-18) Every formula is verified against its source before implementation; the verification source is recorded per method.
  • D-004 (2026-11-18) Every method is documented with its limitations (identifiability, wide intervals, assumptions), not only its computation.
  • D-005 (2026-11-18) Public repository from day one; issues, pull requests and releases; AI use disclosed (see AI_USAGE.md).
  • D-006 (2026-11-18) pkgdown site from the start, one article per method.
  • D-007 (2026-11-18) Numerical tests against published examples and against an independent reference implementation.
  • D-008 (2026-11-18) Code, documentation and commits in English.
  • D-009 (2026-11-19) All package code is written from the verified formulas; third-party code is used only as an external reference for tests, never copied.
  • D-010 (2026-11-20) The bib/ folder (copyrighted papers) is never committed.
  • D-011 (2026-11-24) Impulse-response functions implement both timing conventions found in the literature, selected with the argument same_day_load: “exclude” (sum to n-1; Busso & Chalencon 2023) and “include” (Morton et al. 1990, Eqs. 4-5). Reason: the two forms are not equivalent and both are in use; see MODELS.md, M-01.
  • D-012 (2026-11-24) The default is same_day_load = "exclude". Every fitted object stores and prints its convention, because gains fitted under one convention are not comparable with the other.
  • D-013 (2026-11-24) MODELS.md is the model registry and single source of truth for formulas, verification sources, reference values and literature discrepancies. Its first version (entries M-01 to M-09) was approved by the author on 2026-11-24.
  • D-014 (2026-11-25) The package and the app ship pre-built example datasets modelled on published studies; they are simulated and labelled as simulated. All impulse-response models share one data format (daily load plus performance on some days). The app explains the format and the variables to collect for users who upload their own data.
  • D-015 (2026-11-25) Every day has one of three states: training (load > 0), rest (load = 0), missing (load not available). Days with no row between an athlete’s first and last date are treated as rest by default, with a message listing how many were filled, and a warning when more than 7 consecutive days are filled. The user can request that such days be treated as missing instead.
  • D-016 (2026-11-25) Missing loads are never silently replaced. Descriptors return NA for windows containing a missing day. Impulse-response models refuse to run on series with missing loads unless the user explicitly chooses how to fill them; in the first version the only option is zero.
  • D-017 (2026-11-25) A data file may contain several athletes (optional identifier column) and several load columns; each analysis uses one load column chosen by the user.
  • D-018 (2026-11-26) A second model family, training load -> injury, enters the package from version 0.3: distributed lag non-linear models (wrapping dlnm), the piece-wise exponential additive mixed model with cumulative effects of Zumeta-Olaskoaga et al. 2025 (wrapping pammtools and mgcv), and tools to evaluate predictions (discrimination, calibration). Neural-network and structural-equation approaches are not implemented.
  • D-019 (2026-11-26) Everything related to the acute:chronic workload ratio (ratios, EWMA-based loads, FWF matrices of Matas-Bustos et al. 2025) lives only in the author’s ACWR package. trainingmodels does not reimplement it; the documentation refers to ACWR.
  • D-020 (2026-11-26) Window-based descriptors offer both timing options through same_day_load (“include”: the window ends on the current day; “exclude”: it ends on the previous day, as in Carey et al. 2017, Eq. 1).
  • D-021 (2026-11-26) The default for descriptors is same_day_load = "include". This differs from the impulse-response default (D-012) and must be stated in the help of every descriptor.
  • D-022 (2026-11-26) Monotony and strain: rolling 7-day window computed every day; rest days count as load 0; when all loads in the window are equal the standard deviation is 0 and monotony and strain are NA.

Proposed (architecture, awaiting author approval)

  • A-001 One daily-series class as the single entry point: validates input, sums same-day sessions, marks each day as observed, rest or missing.
  • A-002 Daily-calendar core adapted from the author’s ACWR 0.2.0 package (copied, not imported). ACWR may later become a wrapper.
  • A-003 Shiny app in the same repository, shiny in Suggests.
  • A-004 One exponential-filter engine for all impulse-response models (fitness-only, Banister, fitness delay), computed in recursive form.
  • A-005 Two-level fit: linear regression for baseline and gains, numerical search only over time constants (Busso & Chalencon 2023).
  • A-006 Model comparison with AICc and Akaike weights.
  • A-007 Reference values for tests generated outside the package from the R script of Busso & Chalencon (2023, Supplemental Digital Content 2) and from the dorem package; neither is a dependency.
  • A-008 dlnm and REDI as Suggests, from version 0.3.
  • A-010 The core has no dependencies beyond base R, so that it can run in the browser (Shinylive).
  • A-011 Every function that takes a daily_load validates it first with one internal validator, and returns a plain data frame with one row per row of the input, in the same order (athlete, date, load, then results).

Pending (product and domain, author to decide)

  • P-001 Which outcome students will have for Banister (repeated performance tests or not); whether Banister in the app is simulation plus example data.
  • P-002 Closed 2026-11-25: resolved by D-015 to D-017.
  • P-003 How students access the app (local R or hosted URL).
  • P-004 Language of the theory documentation and of the app interface.
  • P-005 Planned research use in the next six months (JOSS vs JOSE).
  • P-006 Closed 2026-11-24: Morton et al. (1990) was read and uses a different timing convention; resolved by D-011 and D-012.
  • P-007 Include the fitness-only model in the first version.
  • P-008 Every fit reports trivial comparators (mean, straight line).
  • P-009 Fit output foregrounds the response to a single session (curve, t_n, t_g) over individual parameters.
  • P-010 Show half-life alongside time constants.
  • P-011 User declares whether higher or lower performance values are better.
  • P-012 App shows the link between EWMA and Banister without gains.
  • P-013 First version assumes zero initial fitness and fatigue, documented as a limitation.
  • P-014 Ask T. Busso for the swimmers’ dataset.
